contents.html: Abstract
contents.html_ja: 概要

contents.html: The Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP) is a suite of specifications that standardize the format and nomenclature by which software flaw and security configuration information is communicated, both to machines and humans. This publication, along with its annex (NIST Special Publication 800-126Ar4) and a set of schemas, collectively define the technical composition of SCAP version 1.4 in terms of its component specifications, their interrelationships and interoperation, and the requirements for SCAP content.
contents.html_ja: Security Content Automation Protocol（SCAP）は、ソフトウェアの欠陥およびセキュリティ構成情報が機械と人間の両方に伝達される形式と命名法を標準化する一連の仕様群である。本出版物は、その附属書（NIST Special Publication 800-126Ar4）および一連のスキーマとともに、構成仕様、それらの相互関係と相互運用、ならびにSCAPコンテンツの要件の観点から、SCAPバージョン1.4の技術的構成を集合的に定義する。

contents.html: The Information Technology Laboratory (ITL) at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) promotes the U.S. economy and public welfare by providing technical leadership for the Nation’s measurement and standards infrastructure. ITL develops tests, test methods, reference data, proof of concept implementations, and technical analyses to advance the development and productive use of information technology. ITL’s responsibilities include the development of management, administrative, technical, and physical standards and guidelines for the cost-effective security and privacy of other than national security-related information in federal information systems. The Special Publication 800-series reports on ITL’s research, guidelines, and outreach efforts in information system security, and its collaborative activities with industry, government, and academic organizations.

contents.html: Executive Summary
contents.html_ja: エグゼクティブサマリー

contents.html: The Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP) is a suite of specifications that standardize the format and nomenclature by which security configuration information is communicated to both machines and humans.1 SCAP is a multi-purpose framework of specifications that support automated configuration, vulnerability and patch checking, technical and managerial control compliance activities, and security measurement. Goals for the development of SCAP include standardizing system security management, promoting the interoperability of security products, and fostering the use of standard expressions of security content.
contents.html_ja: Security Content Automation Protocol（SCAP）は、セキュリティ構成情報を機械と人間の両方に伝達するためのフォーマットと命名法を標準化する一連の仕様である。1 SCAPは、自動化された構成チェック、脆弱性チェックおよびパッチチェック、技術的および管理的な管理策のコンプライアンス活動、ならびにセキュリティ測定をサポートする仕様の多目的フレームワークである。SCAP策定の目標には、システムセキュリティ管理の標準化、セキュリティ製品の相互運用性の促進、セキュリティコンテンツの標準的な表現の利用推進が含まれる。

contents.html: Security configuration in SCAP format is curated and managed by the NIST National Checklist Program (NCP), which is described in NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-70r5 (Revision 5). This document, its annex [SP800-126Ar4], and a set of schemas collectively define the technical composition of SCAP version 1.4 in terms of its component specifications and requirements. The technical specification for SCAP describes the conventions for ensuring the consistent and accurate exchange of SCAP-conformant content and the ability to reliably use the content with SCAP-conformant products.
contents.html_ja: SCAPフォーマットのセキュリティ構成は、NIST Special Publication（SP）800-70r5（Revision 5）に記載されているNIST National Checklist Program（NCP）によってキュレーションおよび管理されている。本書、その附属書 [SP800-126Ar4]、および一連のスキーマは、構成仕様および要件の観点からSCAPバージョン1.4の技術的構成を集合的に定義している。SCAPの技術仕様は、SCAP適合コンテンツの一貫性のある正確な交換、およびSCAP適合製品でコンテンツを確実に使用できるようにするための規約を記述している。

contents.html: This document, its annex [SP800-126A], and a set of schemas collectively provide the technical specification for version 1.4 of the Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP). SCAP (pronounced /EHS-kap/) consists of a suite of specifications for standardizing the format and nomenclature by which software flaw and security configuration information is communicated to both machines and humans. This document defines requirements for creating and processing SCAP source content that build on the requirements defined within the individual SCAP component specifications. Each new requirement pertains to either using multiple component specifications together or further constraining one of the individual component specifications.2

contents.html: 2. SCAP 1.4 Definition
contents.html_ja: 2. SCAP 1.4の定義

contents.html: In general, SCAP version 1.4 is comprised of 12 component specifications in five categories:
contents.html_ja: 一般に、SCAPバージョン1.4は、5つのカテゴリにおける12のコンポーネント仕様で構成される：

contents.html: Languages. The SCAP languages provide standard vocabularies and conventions for expressing security policies, technical check mechanisms, and assessment results. The SCAP language specifications are the Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format (XCCDF), Open Vulnerability and Assessment Language (OVAL), and Open Checklist Interactive Language (OCIL).
contents.html_ja: 言語。SCAP言語は、セキュリティポリシー、技術的チェックメカニズム、および評価結果を表現するための標準的な語彙と規約を提供する。SCAP言語仕様は、Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format（XCCDF）、Open Vulnerability and Assessment Language（OVAL）、およびOpen Checklist Interactive Language（OCIL）である。

contents.html: Reporting formats. SCAP reporting provides the necessary constructs to express collected information in standardized formats. The SCAP reporting format specifications are Asset Reporting Format (ARF) and Asset Identification. Although Asset Identification is not explicitly a reporting format, SCAP uses it as a key component in identifying the assets that reports relate to.
contents.html_ja: レポート形式。SCAPレポートは、収集された情報を標準化された形式で表現するために必要なコンストラクトを提供する。SCAPレポート形式仕様は、Asset Reporting Format（ARF）およびAsset Identificationである。Asset Identificationは明示的なレポート形式ではないが、SCAPはこれを、レポートが関連するアセットを識別するための主要コンポーネントとして使用している。

contents.html: Identification schemes. The SCAP identification schemes provide a means to identify key concepts, such as software products, vulnerabilities, and configuration items that use standardized identifier formats. They also provide a means to associate individual identifiers with additional data pertaining to the subject of the identifier. The SCAP identification scheme specifications are the Common Platform Enumeration (CPE), Common Configuration Enumeration (CCE), and Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE).
contents.html_ja: 識別スキーム。SCAP識別スキームは、標準化された識別子形式を使用するソフトウェア製品、脆弱性、構成項目などの主要な概念を識別する手段を提供する。また、個々の識別子をその識別子の対象に関する追加データと関連付ける手段も提供する。SCAP識別スキーム仕様は、Common Platform Enumeration（CPE）、Common Configuration Enumeration（CCE）、およびCommon Vulnerabilities and Exposures（CVE）である。

contents.html: Measurement and scoring systems. In SCAP, this refers to evaluating the specific characteristics of a security weakness (e.g., software vulnerabilities and security configuration issues) and generating a score that reflects their relative severity. The SCAP measurement and scoring system specifications are the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) and Common Configuration Scoring System (CCSS).
contents.html_ja: 測定およびスコアリングシステム。SCAPにおいて、これはセキュリティ上の弱点（例：ソフトウェアの脆弱性やセキュリティ設定の問題）の特定の特性を評価し、それらの相対的な深刻度を反映したスコアを生成することを指す。SCAP測定およびスコアリングシステム仕様は、Common Vulnerability Scoring System（CVSS）およびCommon Configuration Scoring System（CCSS）である。

contents.html: Integrity. An SCAP integrity specification helps preserve the integrity of SCAP content and results. The Trust Model for Security Automation Data (TMSAD) is the SCAP integrity specification.
contents.html_ja: 完全性。SCAP完全性仕様は、SCAPコンテンツおよび結果の完全性を維持するのに役立つ。Trust Model for Security Automation Data（TMSAD）がSCAP完全性仕様である。

contents.html: Combinations of these specifications can be used together for particular functions, such as security configuration checking. These functions, known as SCAP use cases, are ways in which a product can use SCAP. The collective XML content used for a use case is called an SCAP data stream, which is a specific instantiation of SCAP content. There are two types of SCAP data streams: an SCAP source data stream holds the input content, and an SCAP result data stream holds the output content. The major elements of a data stream (e.g., an XCCDF benchmark, a set of OVAL definitions) are referred to as stream components.
contents.html_ja: セキュリティ構成チェックなど、特定の機能のために、これらの仕様の組み合わせを一緒に使用することができる。SCAPユースケースとして知られるこれらの機能は、製品がSCAPを使用できる方法である。ユースケースに使用されるXMLコンテンツの集合は、SCAPコンテンツの特定のインスタンス化であるSCAPデータストリームと呼ばれる。SCAPデータストリームには2つのタイプがある。SCAPソースデータストリームは入力コンテンツを保持し、SCAP結果データストリームは出力コンテンツを保持する。データストリームの主要な要素（例：XCCDFベンチマーク、OVAL定義のセット）は、ストリームコンポーネントと呼ばれる。

Another example is a policy mandating that an organization use SCAP source content to perform vulnerability assessments and other security operations.

contents.html: There are two types of SCAP-conformant products: content producers and content consumers. Content producers generate SCAP source data streams. Content consumers accept existing SCAP source data streams, process them, and (when required by the supported use cases) produce SCAP result data streams. Products that claim conformance with the SCAP 1.4 specification SHALL comply with the following requirements:
contents.html_ja: SCAP適合製品には、コンテンツプロデューサーとコンテンツコンシューマーの2つのタイプがある。コンテンツプロデューサーは、SCAPソースデータストリームを生成する。コンテンツコンシューマーは、既存のSCAPソースデータストリームを受け入れて処理し、（サポートされているユースケースで必要な場合）SCAP結果データストリームを生成する。SCAP 1.4仕様への適合を表明する製品は、以下の要件に準拠しなければならない（SHALL comply with）：

contents.html: 1. Adhere to component specifications.

Adhere to the requirements in each applicable SCAP component specification, both for each component that the product implements and for each component required to implement the selected SCAP use cases. The authoritative references for component specifications are listed in [SP800-126A].
2. Implement errata.
Adhere to the requirements in the errata for this document and SP 800-126A that are in effect as of the product’s release date.
3. Producer requirements.

For content producers, generate SCAP source data streams that are (a) XML well-formed, (b) schema-valid per the applicable component specifications, and (c) conformant to the source content conformance requirements in Sec. 2.2 and the use case requirements in Sec. 5.
4. Consumer requirements.

For content consumers, accept and process SCAP source data streams and, when required by the supported use cases, generate SCAP result data streams that are XML well-formed and schema-valid. Content consumers SHALL follow all processing requirements in Sec. 4 for each selected SCAP component specification and each component specification required to implement the selected SCAP use cases and SHALL detect and report non-conformant input.
5. Conformance claim.

Make an explicit claim of conformance to this specification in documentation provided to end users. The claim SHALL identify at least (a) this specification and version (SCAP 1.4), (b) the implemented roles (e.g., producer, consumer), (c) the supported SCAP use cases (Sec. 5), and (d) the implemented SCAP component specifications and versions.

contents.html: This section defines the SCAP 1.4 content syntax, structure, and development requirements and recommendations for SCAP-conformant content and products. Organizations are encouraged to adopt the optional recommendations to promote stronger interoperability and greater content consistency. The first part of the section discusses SCAP source data streams. The middle of the section groups requirements and recommendations by specification: XCCDF, OVAL, OCIL, CPE, CCE, CVE, CVSS, and CCSS, in that order. Finally, the last part of the section discusses applying XML digital signatures to source data streams.

contents.html: An SCAP source data stream collection is composed of SCAP data streams and SCAP source components.7 The components section contains an unbounded number of SCAP source components, each consisting of data expressed using one or more of the SCAP specifications. The data streams section contains one or more source data streams, each of which references the source components that compose the data stream. This model allows source components to be reused across multiple data streams. Many data streams are allowed in a data stream collection to allow for the grouping of related or similar source data streams.
contents.html_ja: SCAPソースデータストリームコレクションは、SCAPデータストリームとSCAPソースコンポーネントで構成される。7 コンポーネントセクションには無制限の数のSCAPソースコンポーネントが含まれ、それぞれが1つ以上のSCAP仕様を使用して表現されたデータで構成されている。データストリームセクションには1つ以上のソースデータストリームが含まれ、それぞれがそのデータストリームを構成するソースコンポーネントを参照する。このモデルにより、複数のデータストリーム間でソースコンポーネントを再利用することが可能になる。データストリームコレクションでは、関連するまたは類似したソースデータストリームをグループ化できるように、多数のデータストリームが許可されている。

In Fig. 1, data stream 1 points to xccdf1, xccdf2, oval1, oval3, cpe dict1, and cpe dict2. Data stream 2 points to xccdf2, oval2, oval3, and cpe dict2. Each data stream is a collection of links to the components it references, represented as <ds:component-ref>. Each component-ref encapsulates the information required to allow the content consumer to connect the components that are embedded in content with the data stream component that should be used. Content authors MAY place components in any order. For example, some authors might choose to place dictionary components first to help optimize data stream parsing.

Links in a <ds:component-ref> element serve two purposes: to indicate which component is being referred to and to provide a map to associate references within a component to other links within the data stream. The latter allows a data stream to define context for each component’s references within the bounds of the data stream’s own set of links. contents.html_ja: 図2において、データストリームは3つのコンポーネントにリンクしている。OVALコンポーネント scap_id_comp_oval1（上記のXML行31〜33を参照）は外部コンテンツを参照しないため、それに対してキャプチャされたマッピングはない。XCCDFコンポーネント（scap_id_comp_xccdf1）（XML行21〜30を参照）およびCPE辞書コンポーネント（scap_id_comp_dict1）（XML行34〜44を参照）は、他のコンポーネント（例：scap_id_cref_ref3）を参照している。

contents.html: When referencing components within the example data stream, a mapping indicates that when scap_id_comp_xccdf1 references “sample-oval-comp,” the content is found through the link to the component identified as “scap_id_comp_oval1” (see XML lines 26, 13, and 18). Similarly, when the scap_id_comp_dict1 component references “dict-oval-comp,” the component reference is resolved through the link to the component identified as “scap_id_comp_oval1” (see XML lines 37, 6, and 18). This approach associates SCAP components within a data stream at the SCAP logical level, allowing components to be reused across data streams within the same data stream collection. This reuse can be accomplished irrespective of how references are made within a given component.
contents.html_ja: 例示されたデータストリーム内のコンポーネントを参照する際、マッピングは、scap_id_comp_xccdf1 が「sample-oval-comp」を参照するときに、そのコンテンツが「scap_id_comp_oval1」として識別されるコンポーネントへのリンクを通じて見つかることを示す（XML行26、13、および18を参照）。同様に、scap_id_comp_dict1 コンポーネントが「dict-oval-comp」を参照するとき、そのコンポーネント参照は「scap_id_comp_oval1」として識別されるコンポーネントへのリンクを通じて解決される（XML行37、6、および18を参照）。このアプローチにより、データストリーム内のSCAPコンポーネントがSCAP論理レベルで関連付けられ、同一のデータストリームコレクション内のデータストリーム間でコンポーネントを再利用できるようになる。この再利用は、特定のコンポーネント内で参照がどのように行われているかに関係なく達成できる。

contents.html: The design of the SCAP source data stream is important for the following reasons:
contents.html_ja: SCAPソースデータストリームの設計は、以下の理由から重要である。

contents.html: Individual components may be developed outside of an SCAP data stream, where linking to other components is not necessarily known when the component is created.
contents.html_ja: 個々のコンポーネントはSCAPデータストリームの外部で開発される場合があり、コンポーネント作成時には他のコンポーネントへのリンクが必ずしも判明しているとは限らない。

contents.html: The SCAP source data stream creates links between different components that were not necessarily designed to reference each other. For example, XCCDF was not designed to reference a particular checking system; it can reference OVAL, OCIL, and other checking systems.
contents.html_ja: SCAPソースデータストリームは、必ずしも相互に参照するように設計されていなかった異なるコンポーネント間にリンクを作成する。例えば、XCCDFは特定のチェックシステムを参照するように設計されたわけではなく、OVAL、OCIL、その他のチェックシステムを参照することができる。

contents.html: The logical link mapping in the data stream places a layer of capability within the data stream to control the dereferencing of URIs within components, creating a complete solution related to bundling components.
contents.html_ja: データストリーム内の論理リンクマッピングは、コンポーネント内のURIの逆参照を制御する機能層をデータストリーム内に配置し、コンポーネントのバンドルに関連する完全なソリューションを作成する。

contents.html: The SCAP source data stream format is intended to be easily adaptable for use in future communication models (e.g., web services, transport protocols, tasking mechanisms).
contents.html_ja: SCAPソースデータストリーム形式は、将来の通信モデル（例：Webサービス、トランスポートプロトコル、タスキングメカニズム）での使用に容易に適応できるように意図されている。

contents.html: The SCAP source data stream format supports more comprehensive validation of component content, including interrelationships between components.
contents.html_ja: SCAPソースデータストリーム形式は、コンポーネント間の相互関係を含む、コンポーネントコンテンツのより包括的な検証をサポートする。

contents.html: The SCAP source data stream collection SHALL validate against the XML schema representation for the source data stream and all associated Schematron schemas. The SCAP components referenced by each <ds:component> and <ds:extended-component> element SHALL validate against the corresponding component schema and its embedded Schematron rules. All of the SCAP-related schemas are referenced at https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/security-content-automation-protocol/scap-releases/scap-1-4. See Sec. 2 in [SP800-126A] for a list of SCAP component schema and Schematron schema locations. These XML and Schematron schemas will be updated if any errors are found. If the old schema links change, updated links will be provided in the annex as errors are corrected.

contents.html: If applicable, each component SHALL validate against its associated Schematron schema. For the SCAP source data stream collection, it SHALL validate against the version of the SCAP Schematron rules as specified on the <ds:data-stream-collection> element’s @schematron-version attribute, and it SHOULD also validate against the latest Schematron rules. NIST provides and maintains a set of Schematron rules to check well-formed SCAP content. The Schematron schemas for the SCAP specification and its applicable component specifications are located at https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/security-content-automation-protocol/scap-releases/scap-1-4. Source content SHOULD pass all Schematron assertions in the Schematron rule files. When creating source content, failed assertions with a “WARNING” or “INFO” flag MAY be disregarded if the assertion discovers an issue in the content that is justifiable and expected based on the needs of the content author. When executing source content, all failed assertions with a “WARNING” or “INFO” flag SHALL be disregarded.
contents.html_ja: 該当する場合、各コンポーネントはその関連するSchematronスキーマに照らして検証しなければならない（SHALL）。SCAPソースデータストリームコレクションについては、<ds:data-stream-collection>要素の@schematron-version属性で指定されているバージョンのSCAP Schematronルールに照らして検証しなければならず（SHALL）、最新のSchematronルールに対しても検証することが推奨される（SHOULD）。NISTは、整形式のSCAPコンテンツをチェックするためのSchematronルールのセットを提供および維持している。SCAP仕様および該当するそのコンポーネント仕様のSchematronスキーマは、https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/security-content-automation-protocol/scap-releases/scap-1-4 に置かれている。ソースコンテンツは、Schematronルールファイル内のすべてのSchematronアサーションに合格すべきである（SHOULD）。ソースコンテンツの作成時、「WARNING」または「INFO」フラグが付いた失敗したアサーションは、コンテンツ作成者のニーズに基づき正当化でき想定内である問題がアサーションによって発見された場合、無視してもよい（MAY）。ソースコンテンツの実行時、「WARNING」または「INFO」フラグが付いた失敗したすべてのアサーションは無視しなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: The Schematron schemas are interpretations of the specifications, and the implementations of their rules are subject to change. Whenever a change is made to a Schematron schema used for this SCAP version, the SCAP Schematron change log document will be updated, and the new Schematron schema will be posted. The latest Schematron schema SHOULD be used in place of any earlier versions. If the latest file is unavailable, the version specified on the <ds:data-stream-collection> element’s @schematron-version attribute SHALL be used instead.

contents.html: Validation tooling: NIST has provided an SCAP Content Validation Tool to assist with checking that SCAP source and result content is well-formed, cross-references resolve, and required values are present. It can report errors and warnings in XML and HTML formats. Use of this or any particular tool is not required for conformance. The tool’s availability, feature set, and maintenance are not guaranteed and may change over time. Products and content authors MAY employ any equivalent validation tool that implements the requirements in this document and the associated component specifications.

Following these rules is not required for conformance, and NIST does not guarantee their availability, accuracy, or maintenance over time. Content authors and product developers MAY employ these or equivalent rule sets as an additional quality-assurance mechanism.

3.2. Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format (XCCDF)
contents.html_ja: 3.2. Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format (XCCDF)

contents.html: This section lists requirements and recommendations for using the Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format (XCCDF) to express an XCCDF benchmark or tailoring component of an SCAP source data stream (see Table 14). They are organized by the following categories: general, <xccdf:Benchmark>, <xccdf:Profile>, <xccdf:Rule>, <xccdf:Value>, and <xccdf:Group>.
3.2.1. General
The @xml:base attribute SHALL NOT be allowed in XCCDF content. This attribute is not compatible with the SCAP data stream model.

Descriptive information within XCCDF MAY be used by SCAP products to assist in selecting the appropriate SCAP data stream, ensure that the most recent or correct version of an XCCDF document is used, and provide additional information about the document. The following requirements and conventions apply to the <xccdf:Benchmark>, <xccdf:Profile>, <xccdf:Value>, <xccdf:Group>, and <xccdf:Rule> elements:
1. One or more instances of the <xccdf:title> element SHALL be provided. Each instance SHALL contain a text value that briefly indicates the purpose of the containing element.
2. One or more instances of the <xccdf:description> element SHALL be provided. Each instance SHALL contain a text value that describes the purpose of the containing element.
XInclude elements SHALL NOT be included in XCCDF content [XINCLUDE].

contents.html: All remaining OPTIONAL elements in the XCCDF schema MAY be included at the author’s discretion unless otherwise noted in this document.

contents.html: The following requirements and recommendations apply to the <xccdf:Benchmark> element:
1. The <xccdf:version> element and the @id attribute SHALL be used together to uniquely identify all revisions of a benchmark.

a. Multiple revisions of a single benchmark SHOULD have the same @id attribute value and different <xccdf:version> element values so that someone who reviews the revisions can readily identify them as multiple versions of a single benchmark.

b. Multiple revisions of a single benchmark SHOULD have <xccdf:version> element values that indicate the revision sequence so that the history of changes from the original benchmark can be determined.
c. The @time attribute of the <xccdf:version> element SHOULD be used for a timestamp of when the benchmark was defined.
2. The @update attribute of the <xccdf:version> element SHOULD be used for a URI that specifies where updates to the benchmark can be obtained.
3. The <xccdf:Benchmark> element SHALL have an @xml:lang attribute.
4. The @style attribute SHOULD have the value “SCAP_1.4.”

5. The <xccdf:status> element SHALL indicate the current status of the benchmark document. The associated text value SHALL be “draft” for documents released in public draft state and “accepted” for documents that have been officially released by an organization. The @date attribute SHALL be populated with the date of the status change. Additional <xccdf:status> elements MAY be included to indicate historic status transitions.

6. The <xccdf:metadata> element SHALL be provided and SHALL, at minimum, contain the Dublin Core [DCES] terms from Table 16. If provided, additional Dublin Core terms SHALL follow the required terms within the element sequence.

contents.html_ja: 3.2.4.3. パッチ最新化ルールの使用

contents.html: An OVAL source data stream component MAY be used to represent a series of checks to verify that patches have been installed. Historically, an XCCDF convention has been used to identify such a reference. An XCCDF benchmark MAY include a patches up-to-date rule that SHALL reference an OVAL source data stream component.

contents.html: When implementing a patches up-to-date XCCDF rule that checks for patches via numerous OVAL patch class definitions, the following approach SHALL be used:

3. Each <xccdf:check-content-ref> element SHALL omit the @name attribute.

4. The @multi-check attribute of the <xccdf:check> element SHALL be set to “true.” This causes a separate <xccdf:rule-result> to be generated for each OVAL patch definition. See Sec. 4.5.2 for more information.

3.2.4.4. CVSS and CCSS Scores
contents.html_ja: 3.2.4.4. CVSSおよびCCSSスコア

contents.html: SCAP 1.0 required the inclusion of static CVSS scores in XCCDF vulnerability-related rules. However, CVSS base scores sometimes change over time (e.g., when more information is available about a particular vulnerability), and CVSS temporal and environmental scores are intended to change to reflect current threats, security controls, and other factors. As a result, the practice of embedding CVSS scores in XCCDF content was no longer required starting with SCAP 1.1.

During scoring, current CVSS scores acquired dynamically, such as from a data feed, SHOULD be used in place of the @weight attribute within XCCDF vulnerability-related rules. Section 3.8 contains additional requirements for CVSS usage.

CCSS scores are more stable than CVSS scores, but they still may change over time. Accordingly, during scoring, current CCSS scores acquired dynamically, such as from a data feed, MAY be used in place of the @weight attribute within XCCDF configuration setting-related rules. Section 3.9 contains additional requirements for CCSS usage.

For both the CVSS and CCSS cases, this specification encourages the use of data feeds that can be updated over time. The specifics around scoring provided in this and referenced sections are intended to prevent potential misuse of the XCCDF @weight attribute within an SCAP data stream.

SCAP 1.4 supports CVSS v3.1 and CVSS v4.0 as defined in [CVSS-3.1] and [CVSS-4.0] respectively, and continues to recognize CVSS v3.0 [CVSS-3.0] and CVSS v2.0 [CVSS-2.0] as legacy versions for pre-existing vulnerability data only. When more than one CVSS score is available for a given vulnerability from an authoritative source (such as the NIST National Vulnerability Database CVE feed referenced in Sec. 3.7), SCAP-conformant products SHOULD apply the version-precedence rule defined in Sec. 3.8 - that is, products SHOULD prefer a CVSS v4.0 score over a CVSS v3.1 score, SHOULD prefer a CVSS v3.1 score over a CVSS v3.0 score, and SHOULD prefer a CVSS v3.0 score over a CVSS v2.0 score. This further supports the use of updatable data feeds to provide current CVSS information. As acknowledged in prior revisions of this specification, XCCDF does not provide a means to indicate which CVSS version was used when calculating an XCCDF score; this is a recognized weakness in the XCCDF specification. As a result, tool developers are encouraged not to rely solely on the scoring information embedded in an SCAP checklist for downstream risk decisions, and SHOULD instead recompute or revalidate CVSS scores against the latest authoritative source at evaluation time.

contents.html: This section lists requirements and recommendations for using the Open Vulnerability and Assessment Language (OVAL) to express an OVAL component of an SCAP source data stream (see Table 14).9 Because SCAP 1.4 supports the use of multiple OVAL source data stream components, an SCAP content creator could choose to divide the OVAL definitions into multiple components. For example, a content creator could create one OVAL source data stream component that contains a set of OVAL definitions for one OVAL version (e.g., 5.10.1) and another set of OVAL definitions for a newer OVAL version (e.g., 5.12) if both versions are valid according to SCAP 1.4 requirements. SCAP 1.4 also supports multiple types of OVAL definitions within a single OVAL source data stream component. For example, a benchmark could reference OVAL compliance and vulnerability definitions contained in a single data stream component.
The version of any particular OVAL document instance SHALL be specified using the <oval:schema_version> content element of the <oval:generator> element, as in this example:
9 See the SCAP 1.4 annex document [SP800-126A] for requirements regarding which OVAL versions shall or may be used in SCAP 1.4 content.

contents.html: <oval:generator> <oval:product_name>The OVAL Repository</oval:product_name> <oval:schema_version>5.12</oval:schema_version> </oval:generator>

The versions that are specified using the <oval:schema_version> content element SHALL correspond to the versions specified by the @xsi:schemaLocation attribute value for the OVAL schema if an @xsi:schemaLocation attribute is specified.

Some OVAL interpreters make use of the OVAL variable format to allow variable values to be passed to the OVAL interpreter. While the OVAL variable format is not part of an SCAP data stream, this format can be used to carry variable information as part of an SCAP product for non-SCAP-related purposes.

“Compliance” if it represents a check for the system’s configuration complying with policy requirements (e.g., having the required value for a specific configuration setting)

contents.html: 1. For compliance class definitions:

contents.html: 2. For inventory class definitions:

contents.html: 3. For patch class definitions:

a. If an OVAL patch class definition is associated with a source-specific identifier (e.g., Knowledge Base numbers for Microsoft patches), these identifiers SHOULD be included in <oval-def:reference> elements contained by the definition. For example:

b. If an OVAL patch class definition maps to one or more CVE identifiers, the definition MAY include <oval-def:reference> elements that reference those identifiers using the following format:
<oval-def:reference source="http://cve.mitre.org" ref_id="CVE_identifier"/>

This recommendation is weaker than its counterparts for the other class definition types because a CVE identifier is not an identifier for a patch; it is more of an association. For example, one patch could fix multiple vulnerabilities, so it would map to multiple CVE identifiers.
The source attribute SHALL be defined using either “http://cve.mitre.org” (preferred method) or “CVE.”
c. Definitions that are directly or indirectly extended SHALL be limited to inventory and patch classes.
contents.html_ja: c. 直接的または間接的に拡張される定義は、インベントリおよびパッチクラスに限定されなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: 4. For vulnerability class definitions:

a. If an OVAL vulnerability class definition maps to one or more CVE identifiers, the definition SHOULD include <oval-def:reference> elements that reference those identifiers using the following format:
<oval-def:reference source="http://cve.mitre.org" ref_id="CVE_identifier"/>
The source attribute SHALL be defined using either “http://cve.mitre.org” (preferred method) or “CVE.”
b. Definitions that are directly or indirectly extended SHALL be limited to inventory and vulnerability classes.
contents.html_ja: b. 直接的または間接的に拡張される定義は、インベントリおよび脆弱性クラスに限定されなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: For miscellaneous class definitions, no additional requirements apply.
contents.html_ja: その他（miscellaneous）クラス定義については、追加の要件は適用されない。

contents.html: 3.4. Open Checklist Interactive Language (OCIL)
contents.html_ja: 3.4. Open Checklist Interactive Language (OCIL)

contents.html: This section lists recommendations for using the Open Checklist Interactive Language (OCIL) to express an OCIL component of an SCAP source data stream (see Table 14).
contents.html_ja: 本セクションでは、SCAPソースデータストリームのOCILコンポーネントを表現するためにOpen Checklist Interactive Language（OCIL）を使用するための推奨事項を列挙する（表14を参照）。

contents.html: OCIL content SHOULD be used to check rules that cannot be fully automated with OVAL. For example, a particular software product may not have an application programming interface (API) that supports OVAL use. Another example is performing a check that requires user interaction, such as asking the user to look up information within a management console or to report a serial number affixed to a computing device. OCIL can also be used to collect a user’s own information, such as whether the user participated in a recent security training session.
contents.html_ja: OVALで完全に自動化できないルールをチェックするには、OCILコンテンツを使用すべきである（SHOULD）。例えば、特定のソフトウェア製品には、OVALの使用をサポートするアプリケーションプログラミングインターフェース（API）がない場合がある。別の例としては、管理コンソール内で情報を検索するようユーザーに求めたり、コンピューティングデバイスに貼付されたシリアル番号を報告するよう求めたりするなど、ユーザーの対話を必要とするチェックの実行が挙げられる。また、OCILは、ユーザーが最近のセキュリティトレーニングセッションに参加したかどうかなど、ユーザー自身の情報を収集するためにも使用できる。

contents.html: If an <ocil:questionnaire> element maps to one or more CCE, CVE, and/or CPE identifiers, it SHOULD include <ocil:reference> elements that reference those identifiers using the corresponding following format:
<ocil:reference href="http://cce.mitre.org">CCE_identifier</ocil:reference>
<ocil:reference href="http://cve.mitre.org">CVE_identifier</ocil:reference>
<ocil:reference href="http://cpe.mitre.org">CPE_identifier</ocil:reference>
3.5. Common Platform Enumeration (CPE)
contents.html_ja: 3.5. 共通プラットフォーム列挙（Common Platform Enumeration: CPE）

contents.html: This section lists requirements and recommendations for using Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) to express a CPE component of an SCAP source data stream (see Table 14). The Official CPE Dictionary data feed10 MAY be used by SCAP components to reference CPE names. If use of the Official CPE Dictionary is impractical, a subset of the dictionary MAY be used instead. Creating the reduced official dictionary involves first identifying every CPE in <xccdf:platform> and <cpe2:fact-ref> elements contained within referenced <cpe2:platform-specification> elements in every benchmark in the data stream. These CPEs SHALL then be matched against every entry in the Official CPE Dictionary using the CPE name matching algorithm [CPE-M]. All CPEs matched in the official dictionary with a result of EQUAL or SUPERSET SHALL be included in the reduced official dictionary.

One or more third-party dictionaries MAY be included in a data stream as well. All such third-party dictionaries SHOULD follow the requirements of the CPE Dictionary specification [CPE-D]. If including an entire third-party dictionary is impractical, a subset of the dictionary MAY be used instead. The reduced dictionary SHALL be created using the same procedure outlined for creating a subset of the official dictionary. In all cases, a dictionary component MAY be remote to the data stream collection.
10 The Official CPE Dictionary is available at https://nvd.nist.gov/products/cpe.
contents.html_ja: 10 公式CPE辞書は https://nvd.nist.gov/products/cpe で入手可能である。

contents.html: Each CPE name [CPE-N] in an <xccdf:platform> or <cpe2:fact-ref> element within an XCCDF document SHALL match at least one CPE entry in a dictionary referenced by the data stream. A match is considered an EQUAL or SUPERSET result when matching the CPE name to a dictionary entry, as defined in the CPE Name Matching specification [CPE-M]. Only non-deprecated names SHOULD be used. Checklist authors SHOULD ensure that each CPE name [CPE-N] they specify in an <xccdf:platform> or <cpe2:fact-ref> element within an XCCDF document has a check associated with its CPE name. If a corresponding check does not exist, then it will not be possible to fully detect the presence of the product and determine platform applicability.

[CPE-D] provides the defining structure of a CPE dictionary. A <cpe2_dict:cpe-item> element MAY contain one or more <cpe2-dict:check> elements that reference OVAL inventory class definitions. The referenced OVAL inventory class definition SHALL specify the technical procedure for determining whether or not a specific target asset is an instance of the CPE name specified by the <cpe2_dict:cpe-item> element. This usage is encouraged for CPE components. If a <cpe2_dict:cpe-item> element contained in a CPE component references an OVAL inventory class definition, then that definition SHALL be resolved by an @href attribute that references an OVAL source data stream component in the same data stream.

Because there may be a lag between when a new product is available and when the Official CPE Dictionary is updated to include a CPE name for that product, third-party dictionaries may be needed to compensate. When creating a subset of the Official CPE Dictionary or a third-party dictionary, a <cpe2_dict:check> element on an entry MAY be added or modified if the existing check does not provide satisfactory content to test the presence of the CPE name.
3.6. Common Configuration Enumeration (CCE)
contents.html_ja: 3.6. 共通構成列挙（CCE）

contents.html: To maintain consistency and accuracy, SCAP content that references a configuration setting SHALL use the official CCE identifier if a CCE entry for a particular configuration setting exists in the official CCE list. If no CCE entry exists for the configuration setting of interest, the content author SHOULD seek to have a CCE identifier issued for the configuration setting. See the OVAL compliance class definition requirements in Sec. 3.3 and the <xccdf:ident> requirements in Sec. 3.2.4.1 for additional requirements regarding CCE identifier references. The current official CCE list is available at https://ncp.nist.gov/cce, and new CCEs can be requested from NIST via email at cce@nist.gov.

Use of an official, dynamic data feed is preferred over the static coding of CCE-related supporting information in SCAP data sources. For example, NVD provides a data feed11 that is the authoritative mapping between CCE identifiers and the control identifiers defined in SP 800-53. Embedding control identifiers within SCAP content is strongly discouraged due to the maintenance burden that it imposes on content maintainers when the control identifiers are revised. A preferred technique is to only embed CCE identifiers in SCAP content. When mappings to SP 800-53 control identifiers are needed, dynamically acquire them from the
11 See https://ncp.nist.gov/cce.
contents.html_ja: 11 https://ncp.nist.gov/cce を参照されたい。

contents.html: official data feed, and associate them with the SCAP content based on its embedded CCE identifiers.
contents.html_ja: 公式データフィード、およびそれらを埋め込まれたCCE識別子に基づいてSCAPコンテンツと関連付ける。

contents.html: 3.7. Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE)
contents.html_ja: 3.7. 共通脆弱性識別子（Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures: CVE）

contents.html: CVE references in SCAP content MAY use any CVE identifier in any non-deprecated state recognized by the CVE Program, including identifiers in the RESERVED state and identifiers in the PUBLISHED state. CVE identifiers in the REJECTED state, and any other deprecated CVE identifiers, SHALL NOT be used.
contents.html_ja: SCAPコンテンツ内のCVE参照は、CVEプログラムが認識する、非推奨ではない（non-deprecated）任意の状態のCVE識別子を使用してよい（MAY）。これには、RESERVED状態の識別子およびPUBLISHED状態の識別子が含まれる。REJECTED状態のCVE識別子、およびその他の非推奨となったCVE識別子は使用してはならない（SHALL NOT）。

contents.html: If a CVE identifier exists for a particular vulnerability, the official CVE identifier SHALL be used. If no CVE exists for the software flaw, an alternate identifier MAY be used, but the content author SHOULD seek to have a CVE identifier issued for the vulnerability. Information on submitting unpublished vulnerabilities and obtaining CVE identifiers is available at https://cve.org.
contents.html_ja: 特定の脆弱性に対してCVE識別子が存在する場合、公式のCVE識別子を使用しなければならない（SHALL）。ソフトウェアの欠陥に対してCVEが存在しない場合、代替識別子を使用してもよいが（MAY）、コンテンツ作成者はその脆弱性に対してCVE識別子が発行されるよう努めるべきである（SHOULD）。未公開の脆弱性の提出およびCVE識別子の取得に関する情報は、https://cve.org で入手可能である。

contents.html: NIST provides public access to current CVE data - including descriptions, CVSS metrics, CPE applicability statements, and weakness (CWE) mappings - through two complementary mechanisms maintained by the National Vulnerability Database (NVD). Both mechanisms emit data conforming to the same JSON 2.0 schema, available at https://csrc.nist.gov/schema/nvd/api/2.0/cve_api_json_2.0.schema.
contents.html_ja: NISTは、National Vulnerability Database（NVD）が維持管理する2つの補完的なメカニズムを通じて、現在のCVEデータ（説明、CVSSメトリクス、CPE適用性ステートメント、および脆弱性タイプ（CWE）のマッピングを含む）へのパブリックアクセスを提供している。両方のメカニズムは、https://csrc.nist.gov/schema/nvd/api/2.0/cve_api_json_2.0.schema で入手可能な同じJSON 2.0スキーマに準拠したデータを出力する。

contents.html: Preferred mechanism - NVD CVE API 2.0. SCAP-conformant tools that consume CVE data dynamically SHOULD use the NVD CVE API 2.0. The API supports lookup by CVE identifier, time-bounded change retrieval (for incremental synchronization), and full enumeration with offset-based pagination. Documentation is available at https://nvd.nist.gov/developers/vulnerabilities, and a general developer on-ramp at https://nvd.nist.gov/developers. Production tools SHOULD register an NVD API key (see https://nvd.nist.gov/developers/request-an-api-key) so that per-source rate limits do not throttle synchronization during normal operation.
contents.html_ja: 推奨メカニズム - NVD CVE API 2.0。CVEデータを動的に利用するSCAP適合ツールは、NVD CVE API 2.0を使用すべきである（SHOULD）。このAPIは、CVE識別子による検索、時間制限付きの変更取得（増分同期用）、およびオフセットベースのページネーションによる完全な列挙をサポートしている。ドキュメントは https://nvd.nist.gov/developers/vulnerabilities で、一般的な開発者向け導入ガイドは https://nvd.nist.gov/developers で入手可能である。本番ツールは、通常動作中に送信元ごとのレート制限によって同期が抑制されないよう、NVD APIキーを登録すべきである（SHOULD）（https://nvd.nist.gov/developers/request-an-api-key を参照）。

contents.html: Supported alternative - NVD JSON 2.0 vulnerability feeds. Tools that perform bulk import or maintain a local mirror MAY consume the JSON 2.0 vulnerability feeds, available at https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/data-feeds. The feeds are organized by CVE-identifier year (file naming ‘nvdcve-2.0-{YYYY}.json.gz’ and ‘.zip’), and additionally include "modified" and "recent" feeds covering changes within the previous eight days. Each feed is accompanied by a ‘.meta’ file (e.g., ‘nvdcve-2.0-{YYYY}.meta’) recording the last-modified timestamp, the uncompressed file size, and a SHA-256 hash of the uncompressed file. SCAP-conformant tools that synchronize via the JSON 2.0 feeds SHALL consult the corresponding ‘.meta’ file before downloading the feed payload, and SHALL NOT re-download a feed whose ‘.meta’ file is unchanged from the prior synchronization. NVD documents that this polling pattern, applied to all year and incremental feeds, results in fewer than 200 requests per day from a single consumer.
contents.html_ja: サポートされる代替手段 - NVD JSON 2.0脆弱性フィード。一括インポートを実行するかローカルミラーを維持するツールは、https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/data-feeds で入手可能なJSON 2.0脆弱性フィードを利用してもよい（MAY）。このフィードはCVE識別子の年別に整理されており（ファイル命名形式は「nvdcve-2.0-{YYYY}.json.gz」および「.zip」）、さらに過去8日以内の変更をカバーする「modified」および「recent」フィードも含まれている。各フィードには、最終更新タイムスタンプ、非圧縮ファイルサイズ、および非圧縮ファイルのSHA-256ハッシュを記録した「.meta」ファイル（例：「nvdcve-2.0-{YYYY}.meta」）が付属している。JSON 2.0フィードを介して同期を行うSCAP適合ツールは、フィードのペイロードをダウンロードする前に対処する「.meta」ファイルを参照しなければならず（SHALL）、前回の同期から「.meta」ファイルが変更されていないフィードを再ダウンロードしてはならない（SHALL NOT）。NVDの文書によれば、すべての年別フィードおよび増分フィードにこのポーリングパターンを適用することで、単一の利用者からのリクエスト数は1日あたり200件未満に抑えられる。

contents.html: CVSS metric fields. The CVE record returned by both the API and the JSON 2.0 feeds carries CVSS metric data in version-specific fields. The field names are ‘cvssMetricV2’ (for CVSS v2.0; the absence of a minor-version digit in this field name is a known irregularity in the NVD schema relative to the v3.x and v4.0 fields), ‘cvssMetricV30’ (CVSS v3.0), ‘cvssMetricV31’ (CVSS v3.1), and ‘cvssMetricV40’ (CVSS v4.0). Sect. 3.8 specifies the SCAP 1.4 version-precedence rule under which SCAP-conformant tools select among these fields when more than one is populated for the same CVE.
contents.html_ja: CVSSメトリクスフィールド。APIとJSON 2.0フィードの両方から返されるCVEレコードには、バージョン固有のフィールドにCVSSメトリクスデータが含まれている。フィールド名は、「cvssMetricV2」（CVSS v2.0用。このフィールド名にマイナーバージョン番号が存在しないことは、v3.xおよびv4.0フィールドに対するNVDスキーマの既知の不規則性である）、「cvssMetricV30」（CVSS v3.0）、「cvssMetricV31」（CVSS v3.1）、および「cvssMetricV40」（CVSS v4.0）である。セクション3.8では、同一のCVEに対してこれら複数のフィールドにデータが入力されている場合に、SCAP適合ツールがどのフィールドを選択するかに関するSCAP 1.4のバージョン優先順位規則を規定している。

contents.html: 3.8. Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS)
contents.html_ja: 3.8. 共通脆弱性評価システム（Common Vulnerability Scoring System: CVSS）

contents.html: The NIST CVE data feed (see Sec. 3.7) is one source of CVSS base scores and vector data that MAY be used by SCAP-conformant products to support additional use cases built on SCAP, and MAY be used along with Threat, Temporal, Environmental, or Supplemental scores and vectors obtained from other authoritative sources.
contents.html_ja: NIST CVEデータフィード（Sec. 3.7を参照）は、SCAP上に構築された追加のユースケースをサポートするためにSCAP適合製品によって使用されてもよい（MAY）CVSS基本スコアおよびベクターデータのソースの1つであり、他の信頼できる情報源から取得された脅威、現状、環境、または補足のスコアおよびベクターとともに使用されてもよい（MAY）。

contents.html: 3.8.1. Supported CVSS Versions
contents.html_ja: 3.8.1. サポートされているCVSSバージョン

contents.html: SCAP 1.4 recognizes four CVSS versions, organized into two tiers:
contents.html_ja: SCAP 1.4は、2つの階層に編成された4つのCVSSバージョンを認識する:

contents.html: Current versions (for new SCAP content):
contents.html_ja: 現行バージョン（新規SCAPコンテンツ用）:

contents.html: CVSS v4.0 [CVSS-4.0] - preferred. SCAP-conformant content authored after the publication date of SP 800-126r4 SHOULD reference CVSS v4.0 vectors and scores when such data is available from an authoritative source.
CVSS v3.1 [CVSS-3.1] - supported. CVSS v3.1 vectors and scores SHALL be accepted by SCAP-conformant products when no CVSS v4.0 data is available for the referenced vulnerability.
Legacy versions (for pre-existing data only):
contents.html_ja: レガシーバージョン（既存のデータのみ対象）:

contents.html: CVSS v3.0 [CVSS-3.0] - legacy. CVSS v3.0 vectors and scores MAY be referenced solely for vulnerabilities published prior to 10 September 2019 (the date on which the NVD officially adopted CVSS v3.1 guidance for all new and re-analyzed CVEs) and only when neither a CVSS v3.1 nor a CVSS v4.0 vector has been issued for the same vulnerability.

CVSS v2.0 [CVSS-2.0] - legacy. CVSS v2.0 vectors and scores MAY be referenced solely for vulnerabilities published prior to 13 July 2022 (the date on which the NVD ceased generating new CVSS v2.0 vector strings) and only when no CVSS v3.0, v3.1, or v4.0 vector has been issued for the same vulnerability.

SCAP-conformant products SHALL identify the source CVSS version from the vector-string prefix where available - ‘CVSS:4.0/’, ‘CVSS:3.1/’, or ‘CVSS:3.0/’ - and SHALL NOT silently relabel a vector under a different version. Vectors lacking a ‘CVSS:’ prefix SHALL be treated as CVSS v2.0.
contents.html_ja: SCAP適合製品は、利用可能な場合、ベクターストリングのプレフィックス（「CVSS:4.0/」、「CVSS:3.1/」、または「CVSS:3.0/」）からソースのCVSSバージョンを識別しなければならず（SHALL）、ベクターを異なるバージョンで暗黙的にラベル付け直してはならない（SHALL NOT）。「CVSS:」プレフィックスがないベクターは、CVSS v2.0として扱わなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: 3.8.2. Version Precedence
contents.html_ja: 3.8.2. バージョンの優先順位

contents.html: When more than one CVSS vector is available for the same vulnerability, SCAP-conformant products SHOULD select the version with the highest major number first, breaking ties on minor number. The resulting precedence is:

Products SHOULD record, alongside any CVSS score they emit, the CVSS version, the vector string, and the source (e.g., the NVD CVE feed entry identifier) so that downstream consumers can rederive or recompute the score against the authoritative source.
contents.html_ja: 下流の利用者が信頼できる情報源に照らしてスコアを再導出または再計算できるように、製品は出力する任意のCVSSスコアとともに、CVSSバージョン、ベクターストリング、および情報源（例：NVD CVEフィードのエントリ識別子）を記録すべきである（SHOULD）。

contents.html: 3.8.3. Metric Groups
contents.html_ja: 3.8.3. メトリックグループ

contents.html: Products consuming CVSS v4.0 data SHOULD support the four metric groups defined by [CVSS-4.0] - Base, Threat, Environmental, and Supplemental - and SHOULD preserve any nomenclature qualifier (CVSS-B, CVSS-BT, CVSS-BE, CVSS-BTE) reported by the source. Products consuming CVSS v3.1 or v3.0 data SHOULD support the three metric groups defined by [CVSS-3.1] / [CVSS-3.0] - Base, Temporal, and Environmental. Products consuming CVSS v2.0 data SHOULD support the three metric groups defined by [CVSS-2.0] - Base, Temporal, and Environmental.
contents.html_ja: CVSS v4.0データを利用する製品は、[CVSS-4.0]で定義されている4つのメトリックグループ（基本（Base）、脅威（Threat）、環境（Environmental）、および補足（Supplemental））をサポートすべきであり（SHOULD）、情報源から報告された命名法の修飾子（CVSS-B、CVSS-BT、CVSS-BE、CVSS-BTE）を保持すべきである（SHOULD）。CVSS v3.1またはv3.0データを利用する製品は、[CVSS-3.1] / [CVSS-3.0]で定義されている3つのメトリックグループ（基本（Base）、現状（Temporal）、および環境（Environmental））をサポートすべきである（SHOULD）。CVSS v2.0データを利用する製品は、[CVSS-2.0]で定義されている3つのメトリックグループ（基本（Base）、現状（Temporal）、および環境（Environmental））をサポートすべきである（SHOULD）。

contents.html: 3.8.4. Known Limitation in XCCDF
contents.html_ja: 3.8.4. XCCDFにおける既知の制限事項

contents.html: As noted in sect. 3.2.4.4, XCCDF does not provide a means to indicate which CVSS version was used when calculating an XCCDF score. SCAP-conformant tools that emit XCCDF results SHOULD therefore record the CVSS version and vector for each rule out-of-band (for example, in the corresponding ARF report or in tool-specific extensions) so that the version is recoverable by downstream consumers. This limitation is preserved from prior SCAP revisions and is not resolved by SCAP 1.4.
contents.html_ja: セクション 3.2.4.4 で言及されているように、XCCDF は XCCDF スコアの計算時にどの CVSS バージョンが使用されたかを示す手段を提供していない。したがって、XCCDF 結果を出力する SCAP 適合ツールは、ダウンストリームの利用者がバージョンを復元できるように、各ルールの CVSS バージョンとベクターをアウトオブバンド（例えば、対応する ARF レポート内やツール固有の拡張機能内など）で記録すべきである（SHOULD）。この制限は以前の SCAP リビジョンから維持されており、SCAP 1.4 でも解決されていない。

contents.html: 3.9. Common Configuration Scoring System (CCSS)
contents.html_ja: 3.9. 共通設定スコアリングシステム（CCSS）

contents.html: CCSS base, temporal, and environmental scores and vectors MAY be used by products. Adopters should consider CCSS data in the context of organizational security policies and dependencies among vulnerabilities. See [CCSS] for additional information.
contents.html_ja: 製品は CCSS のベーススコア、現状スコア（temporal scores）、環境スコアおよびベクターを使用してよい（MAY）。採用者は、組織のセキュリティポリシーおよび脆弱性間の依存関係の文脈において CCSS データを考慮すべきである。追加情報については [CCSS] を参照のこと。

contents.html: 3.10. XML Digital Signature
contents.html_ja: 3.10. XML デジタル署名

contents.html: Digitally signing source data streams helps ensure the integrity and trustworthiness of legitimate content by preventing unauthorized content from being processed. Leveraging the TMSAD specification [TMSAD] for SCAP improves the legitimacy of authoritative content. Content authors SHOULD digitally sign SCAP source data stream collections in accordance with [TMSAD] and the requirements provided in this section.
contents.html_ja: ソースデータストリームにデジタル署名を行うことは、未承認のコンテンツが処理されるのを防ぐことで、正当なコンテンツの完全性と信頼性を確保するのに役立つ。SCAP に TMSAD 仕様 [TMSAD] を活用することで、信頼できるコンテンツの正当性が向上する。コンテンツ作成者は、[TMSAD] および本セクションで提供される要件に従って、SCAP ソースデータストリームコレクションにデジタル署名すべきである（SHOULD）。

contents.html: 3.10.1. Signature Location
contents.html_ja: 3.10.1. 署名の位置

contents.html: If a digital signature is included in a source data stream collection, it SHALL be placed as the last element within the source data stream collection root element.

contents.html_ja: 3.10.2. 署名の表現

contents.html: or
contents.html_ja: または

contents.html: c) If the <ds:Signature> element targets a single data stream, then the <ds:SignedInfo> element SHALL contain a same-document reference (e.g., #id) that resolves to the data stream collection being signed along with either:

contents.html: 4. SCAP Content Processing Requirements and Recommendations

This section defines the processing requirements that SCAP content consumers SHOULD follow to correctly process SCAP 1.4 content. This section also provides recommendations that content producers and consumers are encouraged to adopt to promote stronger interoperability and greater consistency.
contents.html_ja: 本セクションでは、SCAP 1.4コンテンツを正しく処理するためにSCAPコンテンツコンシューマが従うべき（SHOULD）処理要件を定義する。また、本セクションでは、より強力な相互運用性と高い一貫性を促進するために、コンテンツプロデューサおよびコンシューマが採用することが推奨される推奨事項も示す。

contents.html: 4.1. Legacy Support
contents.html_ja: 4.1. レガシーサポート

contents.html: Content consumers that support SCAP 1.4 may be interested in supporting earlier version of SCAP (i.e., SCAP 1.3) if there is little difference between the two content streams.12 Content consumers that process legacy SCAP content SHOULD be capable of outputting results in the current SCAP revision. Additionally, content consumers MAY output results in the same SCAP version as the source content. For producers of results in legacy formats, legacy results MAY also be converted into results based on the current SCAP revision.

Certain constructs can be deprecated in the SCAP component specifications.13 SCAP content consumers SHOULD support deprecated constructs unless specifically noted in the annex because they are still valid in SCAP 1.4 and supported legacy SCAP versions. This recommendation ensures that legacy SCAP content that uses these deprecated constructs will continue to be supported.
Content consumers that support OVAL SHOULD support OVAL definition documents written against all versions of OVAL component specifications listed in the annex.
contents.html_ja: OVALをサポートするコンテンツコンシューマーは、付属文書に記載されているOVALコンポーネント仕様のすべてのバージョンに対して作成されたOVAL定義文書をサポートすべきである（SHOULD）。

contents.html: 4.2. Source Data Streams
contents.html_ja: 4.2. ソースデータストリーム

contents.html: Content consumers SHALL be capable of validating SCAP content against the appropriate schemas and Schematron stylesheets, detecting and reporting errors, and failing gracefully if there are errors. The relevant XML schemas and Schematron rule sets are available at https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/security-content-automation-protocol/scap-releases/scap-1-4. See Sec. 3.1 for additional information on the Schematron rule sets.

Content consumers SHOULD validate XML digital signatures if they exist in the content. Validating a signature includes confirming that the signature value is valid, all of the reference hashes in the signature and manifest are correct, and the public key used to verify the signature is from a trusted source. A data stream with a signature that does not validate SHOULD NOT be evaluated by a content consumer.
contents.html_ja: コンテンツコンシューマーは、コンテンツ内にXMLデジタル署名が存在する場合、それを検証すべきである（SHOULD）。署名の検証には、署名値が有効であること、署名およびマニフェスト内のすべての参照ハッシュが正しいこと、ならびに署名の検証に使用された公開鍵が信頼できる送信元からのものであることを確認することが含まれる。検証に合格しない署名を持つデータストリームは、コンテンツコンシューマーによって評価されるべきではない（SHOULD NOT）。

contents.html: When a <ds:extended-component> that is not recognized by the tool is referenced from a <ds:data-stream>, <ds:component>, or <ds:extended-component> element, the tool SHALL issue a warning.

If more than one <ds:data-stream> element is specified on the <ds:data-stream-collection>, the ID of the <ds:data-stream> to execute SHALL be indicated to the content consumer, and the content consumer SHALL use the specified <ds:data-stream>. If more than one <xccdf:Benchmark> is referenced by a <ds:data-stream>, the ID of the <xccdf:Benchmark> to execute SHALL be indicated to the content consumer, and the content consumer SHALL process the indicated <xccdf:Benchmark>. Because SCAP and its component specifications do not formally define how to designate a particular data stream or benchmark, it is expected that products will implement these capabilities in a proprietary way.
12 See https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/126/r2/final (SCAP 1.2) and https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/126/r3/final (SCAP 1.3).

contents.html: 4.3. XCCDF Processing
contents.html_ja: 4.3. XCCDF処理

contents.html: The following requirements and recommendations pertain to content consumers processing XCCDF benchmark and tailoring components from an SCAP source data stream.
contents.html_ja: 以下の要件および推奨事項は、SCAPソースデータストリームからのXCCDFベンチマークおよびテーラリングコンポーネントを処理するコンテンツコンシューマーに関するものである。

contents.html: 4.3.1. CPE Applicability Processing
contents.html_ja: 4.3.1. CPE適用可能性処理

contents.html: CPEs referenced in an <xccdf:platform> element directly or by a <cpe2:fact-ref> contained within a referenced <cpe2:platform-specification> element SHALL be evaluated as follows to determine their presence on a machine:
contents.html_ja: <xccdf:platform>要素で直接、または参照される<cpe2:platform-specification>要素内に含まれる<cpe2:fact-ref>によって参照されるCPEは、マシン上での存在を判断するために以下のように評価されなければならない（SHALL）：

contents.html: The CPE SHALL be matched against all CPEs in all of the dictionaries referenced by the <ds:data-stream> element. All CPEs that return an EQUAL or SUPERSET result as defined in CPE Name Matching [CPE-M] SHALL be used in evaluating the <xccdf:platform> or <cpe2:fact-ref>.
contents.html_ja: CPEは、<ds:data-stream>要素によって参照されるすべての辞書内のすべてのCPEと照合されなければならない（SHALL）。CPE Name Matching [CPE-M]で定義されているEQUALまたはSUPERSETの結果を返す全CPEは、<xccdf:platform>または<cpe2:fact-ref>の評価に使用されなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: Either a list of CPEs found on the target asset SHALL be known before the scan, or a list SHALL be generated. If a previously known list is used, it SHALL be equivalent to a newly generated list. To generate the list, the <cpe2_dict:check> element data associated with the found <cpe2_dict:cpe-item> elements SHALL be evaluated against the target using the referenced OVAL inventory class definition. If a <cpe2_dict:check> returns “pass,” then the corresponding CPE SHALL be added to the list of CPEs found on the target.
contents.html_ja: ターゲットアセット上で検出されたCPEのリストをスキャン前に把握しておかなければならない（SHALL）か、リストを生成しなければならない（SHALL）。以前から判明しているリストを使用する場合、それは新しく生成されたリストと同等でなければならない（SHALL）。リストを生成するには、検出された<cpe2_dict:cpe-item>要素に関連付けられた<cpe2_dict:check>要素データを、参照されるOVALインベントリクラス定義を使用してターゲットに対して評価しなければならない（SHALL）。<cpe2_dict:check>が「pass」を返した場合、対応するCPEはターゲット上で検出されたCPEのリストに追加されなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: The list of CPEs found on the target asset and either the <xccdf:platform> or the <cpe2:platform-specification> SHALL be used as input to the CPE Applicability Language [CPE-L] algorithm to determine the XCCDF benchmark applicability to the target asset.
contents.html_ja: ターゲットアセットに対するXCCDFベンチマークの適用可能性を判断するために、ターゲットアセット上で検出されたCPEのリスト、および<xccdf:platform>または<cpe2:platform-specification>のいずれかがCPE Applicability Language [CPE-L]アルゴリズムへの入力として使用されなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: 4.3.2. Checking System Usage
contents.html_ja: 4.3.2. チェックシステムの利用

contents.html: If an XCCDF component has multiple <xccdf:check-content-ref> elements, then check processing SHOULD be performed according to [XCCDF:7.2.3.5.1] with the following changes:
contents.html_ja: XCCDFコンポーネントが複数の<xccdf:check-content-ref>要素を持つ場合、チェック処理は以下の変更を加えた上で[XCCDF:7.2.3.5.1]に従って実行されるべきである（SHOULD）。

contents.html: 1. For each <xccdf:check-content-ref> element, a content consumer either SHALL attempt to retrieve the document referenced by the <ds:component-ref> element that is referenced directly by the <xccdf:check-content-ref> element’s @href attribute, or it SHALL resolve the @href attribute within the context of the XML Catalog specified as part of the <ds:component-ref> element used to reference this benchmark. If not resolvable, the next available <xccdf:check-content-ref> element SHALL be evaluated. If none of the <xccdf:check-content-ref> elements are resolvable, then the result of the rule evaluation SHALL be the XCCDF “notchecked” status, and processing of the check SHALL end.

contents.html: 4.5. XCCDF Results
contents.html_ja: 4.5. XCCDF結果

contents.html: The following requirements and recommendations pertain to content consumers that generate XCCDF result data stream components.
contents.html_ja: 以下の要件および推奨事項は、XCCDF結果データストリームコンポーネントを生成するコンテンツコンシューマーに関するものである。

contents.html: Each XCCDF result data stream component SHALL comply with the XCCDF Results schema.
contents.html_ja: 各XCCDF結果データストリームコンポーネントは、XCCDF Resultsスキーマに準拠しなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: XCCDF test results SHALL be documented as the contents of an <xccdf:TestResult> element. To be considered valid SCAP result content, the <xccdf:TestResult> element SHALL meet the following conditions:
1. The @start-time and @end-time attributes SHALL be provided to indicate when the scan started and completed, respectively.
2. The @test-system attribute SHALL be provided, and it SHALL be a CPE name value indicating the product that was responsible for generating the results.
3. When the <xccdf:TestResult> is the root XCCDF element, then it will include an <xccdf:benchmark> element [XCCDF:6.6.2].
a. The <xccdf:benchmark> element SHALL have an @id attribute specified. The @id attribute SHALL match the value of the <xccdf:Benchmark> element’s @id attribute that was processed.

b. The <xccdf:benchmark> element SHALL have an @href attribute specified. The @href attribute SHALL hold the URI that references the XCCDF component (i.e., either local to the data stream collection or remote) that was processed. The URI SHALL be in the form specified for the @href attribute in Table 8.

4. If a child profile of an <xccdf:Tailoring> element was applied during processing, then the <xccdf:tailoring-file> element SHALL be present and SHALL provide the following information about the <xccdf:Tailoring> element: @href, @id, @version, and @time. The @href attribute SHALL hold the URI to the XCCDF tailoring component and SHALL comply with the format described above (item 3).
5. The <xccdf:Profile> element SHALL be included if a profile was applied during processing. This is also applicable to selected profiles that are part of <xccdf:Tailoring>.

6. Regarding the definition and use of <xccdf:Profile> elements, reported <xccdf:set-value> elements SHALL include all those values that are exported by the reported rules. The specific settings are those determined by the reported <xccdf:Profile>.
7. The <xccdf:identity> element SHALL identify the security principal used to access rule evaluations on the targets. This will include the identity name or username used to perform the evaluation.
8. Each IP address associated with the <xccdf:target> SHALL be enumerated using the <xccdf:target-address> element.

9. An <xccdf:target-id-ref> SHALL be specified with a @system attribute of “http://scap.nist.gov/schema/asset-identification/1.1”, an @href attribute value of “”, and a @name attribute value of the ID of the <ai:asset> element in the ARF that this <xccdf:TestResult> is about.

10. The <xccdf:rule-result> elements report the result of the application of each selected rule [XCCDF:6.6.2]. The @role, @severity, and @weight attributes of the <xccdf:rule-result> element SHALL be provided to indicate the values used during assessment. The <xccdf:check/xccdf:check-content-ref> element SHALL record the reference to the checking system-specific result component report ID and check name within the result file using the @href and @name attributes, respectively. The @href attribute SHALL contain “#” and the @id of the <arf:report> that contains the check result. This approach provides traceability between XCCDF and check results. If @multi-check is not set to “true,” and the <xccdf:rule-result> represents a group of checks, then the @name attribute SHALL be omitted. See the example below the next requirement.
contents.html_ja: 10. <xccdf:rule-result> 要素は、選択された各ルールの適用の結果を報告する [XCCDF:6.6.2]。アセスメント中に使用された値を示すために、<xccdf:rule-result> 要素の @role、@severity、および @weight 属性を提供しなければならない（SHALL）。<xccdf:check/xccdf:check-content-ref> 要素は、それぞれ @href 属性および @name 属性を使用して、結果ファイル内の検査システム固有の結果コンポーネントレポートIDおよび検査名への参照を記録しなければならない（SHALL）。@href 属性には、「#」と、検査結果を含む <arf:report> の @id を含めなければならない（SHALL）。このアプローチにより、XCCDFと検査結果の間の追跡可能性が提供される。@multi-check が「true」に設定されておらず、かつ <xccdf:rule-result> が検査のグループを表している場合、@name 属性は省略しなければならない（SHALL）。次の要件の下にある例を参照のこと。

contents.html: 4.5.1. Assigning Identifiers to Rule Results

The <xccdf:rule-result> element provides data that indicates the result of assessing a system using the identified <xccdf:Rule> element. If the target <xccdf:Rule> identified by the <xccdf:rule-result> element’s @idref attribute has one or more <xccdf:ident> elements with a @system attribute value listed in Sec. 3.2.4.1, then each <xccdf:ident> element SHALL also appear within the <xccdf:rule-result> element.

If the <xccdf:ident> element is included, it is important for tracking purposes that produced XCCDF results have specific meanings. If an <xccdf:ident> element is present, and it identifies a CVE, CCE, or CPE entry, then an <xccdf:rule-result> of “pass” SHALL indicate that the check content evaluated within the rule complied with one of the following:
For a CVE entry, the target platform satisfies all of the conditions of the XCCDF rule and is unaffected by the vulnerability or exposure referenced by the CVE.
contents.html_ja: CVEエントリの場合、ターゲットプラットフォームがXCCDFルールのすべての条件を満たし、かつそのCVEによって参照される脆弱性またはエクスポージャーの影響を受けないこと。

contents.html: For a CCE entry, the target platform complies with the configuration-setting guidance expressed in the XCCDF rule.
contents.html_ja: CCEエントリの場合、ターゲットプラットフォームがXCCDFルールで示される設定ガイダンスに準拠していること。

contents.html: For a CPE entry, the target platform was identified on the system.
contents.html_ja: CPEエントリの場合、ターゲットプラットフォームがシステム上で特定されたこと。

contents.html: These interpretations of <xccdf:ident> elements must be preserved. For example, consider two policy recommendations. One is that a particular piece of software be installed, and the second is that another piece of software should not be installed. Both rules for these policy recommendations could use the same CPE entry in their <xccdf:ident> elements. However, because the interpretation of a CPE entry is that a “pass” result indicates that software was installed, the second policy recommendation’s rule would violate this. This can be corrected by using the @con:negate attribute, which is a Boolean attribute that inverts the rule result. The second rule could check for the software being installed and then negate that result, thus giving a result that is consistent in meaning with the first rule. For rules that cannot have their interpretations preserved through the use of the @con:negate attribute, an alternative is to have a CCE entry correspond to the recommendation. Rules that do not use <xccdf:ident> elements have no such restrictions.
4.5.2. Mapping OVAL Results to XCCDF Results
contents.html_ja: 4.5.2. OVAL結果からXCCDF結果へのマッピング

contents.html: When evaluating an <xccdf:Rule> element that references an OVAL definition, the <xccdf:rule-result> element SHALL be used to capture the result of this evaluation. This result SHALL be determined by evaluating the referenced OVAL definition on a target host. The resulting value of an individual <xccdf:check> SHALL be mapped from the OVAL definition result produced during evaluation. The corresponding <xccdf:rule-result/xccdf:result> value is then computed based on the result values of all relevant <xccdf:check> elements.15 While the OVAL specification permits limiting result status reporting, SCAP-conformant content SHALL provide full status reporting, including error, unknown, not applicable, not evaluated, true, and false.

15 Normally, only a single <xccdf:check> element is needed. However, if an <xccdf:complex-check> element is used, there may be multiple results that must be combined, as outlined in the XCCDF specification.
contents.html_ja: 15 通常は、単一の<xccdf:check>要素のみが必要である。ただし、<xccdf:complex-check>要素が使用される場合、XCCDF仕様に概説されているように、結合しなければならない複数の結果が存在する場合がある。

contents.html: Content consumers SHALL apply the mapping illustrated in Table 23 when deriving <xccdf:check> results from OVAL definition processing.
contents.html_ja: コンテンツコンシューマーは、OVAL定義の処理から<xccdf:check>結果を導出する際、表23に示すマッピングを適用しなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: Table 23. Deriving XCCDF check results from OVAL definition results
contents.html_ja: 表23. OVAL定義結果からのXCCDFチェック結果の導出

contents.html_ja: OVAL定義結果 XCCDFチェック結果 XCCDFチェック結果（@negateが「false」に設定されている場合） （@negateが「true」に設定されている場合） error error error unknown unknown unknown not applicable notapplicable notapplicable not evaluated notchecked notchecked 定義クラス 定義結果 compliance true vulnerability false pass fail inventory true patch false 定義クラス 定義結果 compliance False vulnerability true fail pass inventory false patch true

contents.html: The corresponding result value SHALL be recorded based on the @class attribute of the OVAL definition and the @negate attribute of the <xccdf:check> element, where applicable.
contents.html_ja: 該当する場合、対応する結果値は、OVAL定義の@class属性および<xccdf:check>要素の@negate属性に基づいて記録されなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: The mappings in Table 23 are specific to each OVAL definition class. For example, if an OVAL compliance class definition is processed, and OVAL returns a result of “true,” the content consumer is conveying the fact that the system was found to be compliant with that check and therefore returns a “pass” result for that check. A similar definition for a vulnerable condition will return results of “false” if that vulnerability was not found on the examined devices, resulting in a “pass” from the XCCDF check. Negations of check results or their combination in complex checks may result in additional modification before the final corresponding <xccdf:rule-result/xccdf:result> value is known.
contents.html_ja: 表23のマッピングは、各OVAL定義クラスに固有のものである。例えば、OVALコンプライアンスクラスの定義が処理され、OVALが「true」の結果を返した場合、コンテンツコンシューマーはシステムがそのチェックに準拠していると判断されたという事実を伝えており、したがってそのチェックに対して「pass」結果を返す。脆弱な状態に関する同様の定義では、検査されたデバイスでその脆弱性が見つからなかった場合に「false」の結果が返され、XCCDFチェックからは「pass」となる。チェック結果の否定や複合チェックにおけるそれらの結合により、対応する最終的な<xccdf:rule-result/xccdf:result>値が判明する前に追加の変更が生じる場合がある。

contents.html: If the <xccdf:Rule> element under evaluation has an <xccdf:check-content-ref> element with the @name attribute omitted and an <xccdf:check> element with its @multi-check attribute set to “true,” then the result of each evaluated OVAL definition SHALL be recorded as a separate <xccdf:rule-result> element. In this case, the <xccdf:rule-result>/<xccdf:check-content-ref> element SHALL identify the specific check result of each evaluated OVAL definition using the @href and @name attributes, as described in Sec. 4.5, item 8.
contents.html_ja: 評価対象の<xccdf:Rule>要素に@name属性が省略された<xccdf:check-content-ref>要素があり、かつ@multi-check属性が「true」に設定された<xccdf:check>要素がある場合、評価された各OVAL定義の結果は個別の<xccdf:rule-result>要素として記録されなければならない（SHALL）。この場合、セクション4.5の項目8で説明されているように、<xccdf:rule-result>/<xccdf:check-content-ref>要素は、@hrefおよび@name属性を使用して評価された各OVAL定義の特定のチェック結果を識別しなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: According to [XCCDF:Table 9;Table 35;Table 39], if the <xccdf:Rule> element under evaluation is selected, and its @role attribute is set to ”unchecked,” then the rule result SHALL be set to “notchecked.” If the <xccdf:Rule> element under evaluation is selected, and its @role attribute is set to “unscored,” then the rule result SHALL be set to “informational.”
contents.html_ja: [XCCDF:Table 9;Table 35;Table 39]によれば、評価対象の<xccdf:Rule>要素が選択されており、その@role属性が「unchecked」に設定されている場合、ルール結果は「notchecked」に設定されなければならない（SHALL）。評価対象の<xccdf:Rule>要素が選択されており、その@role属性が「unscored」に設定されている場合、ルール結果は「informational」に設定されなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: 4.6. OVAL Results
contents.html_ja: 4.6. OVAL結果

contents.html: The following requirements and recommendations pertain to content consumers that generate OVAL result data stream components. See the annex for additional requirements and recommendations.
contents.html_ja: 以下の要件および推奨事項は、OVAL結果データストリームコンポーネントを生成するコンテンツコンシューマーに関連する。追加の要件および推奨事項については附属書を参照のこと。

contents.html: Each OVAL result data stream component SHALL validate against at least one version of the OVAL results schema that corresponds to an OVAL component specification version that was specified in Sect. 2 of the annex, regardless of the version of the OVAL definitions document that was evaluated.
contents.html_ja: 評価されたOVAL定義文書のバージョンにかかわらず、各OVAL結果データストリームコンポーネントは、附属書のセクション2で指定されたOVALコンポーネント仕様バージョンに対応するOVAL結果スキーマの少なくとも1つのバージョンに対して検証されなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: An SCAP OVAL result data stream component SHALL include the results of every OVAL definition used to generate the reported results.
contents.html_ja: SCAP OVAL結果データストリームコンポーネントは、報告された結果の生成に使用されたすべてのOVAL定義の結果を含まなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: In order to be SCAP-conformant, an SCAP content consumer SHALL be able to produce all types of OVAL result outputs described below. The specific result output SHALL be configurable within the SCAP content consumer.
contents.html_ja: SCAPに準拠するために、SCAPコンテンツコンシューマーは、以下で説明するすべてのタイプのOVAL結果出力を生成できなければならない（SHALL）。特定の結果出力は、SCAPコンテンツコンシューマー内で設定可能でなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: In order to support SCAP instances where OVAL thin content (i.e., only the ID of the definition and the results) is preferred, SCAP content consumers SHALL support all valid values for the <oval-res:directives> that control the expected content of the results file.

To support the ability for results to be consumed by appropriate products, data results SHALL be expressed as a single machine without system characteristics, single machine with system characteristics, or single machine with thin results as follows:
contents.html_ja: 適切な製品によって結果が消費される機能をサポートするために、データ結果は以下のように、システム特性のない単一マシン、システム特性のある単一マシン、またはシン結果を持つ単一マシンとして表現されなければならない（SHALL）：

contents.html: 1. Single machine without system characteristics — A single result file that includes the results of all OVAL definitions evaluated and “full” result types, as described in the <oval-res:ContentEnumeration> element, without system characteristics.
For this format, the values for the <oval-res:directives> element SHALL be:

<oval-res:directives include_source_definitions="false"> <oval-res:definition_true content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_false content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_unknown content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_error content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_not_evaluated content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_not_applicable content="full" reported="true"/> </oval-res:directives>

When creating the OVAL system characteristics, as defined by the <oval-sc:oval_system_characteristics> element, the <oval-sc:collected_objects> and <oval-sc:system_data> elements SHALL NOT be provided.

2. Single machine with system characteristics — A single result file that includes the results of all OVAL definitions evaluated and “full” result types, as described in the <oval-res:ContentEnumeration> element and the system characteristics of the target evaluated.
For this format, the values for the <oval-res:directives> element SHALL be:

<oval-res:directives include_source_definitions="false"> <oval-res:definition_true content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_false content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_unknown content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_error content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_not_evaluated content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_not_applicable content="full" reported="true"/> </oval-res:directives>
When creating the OVAL system characteristics, as defined by the <oval-sc:oval_system_characteristics> element, the <oval-sc:collected_objects> and <oval-sc:system_data> elements SHALL be provided.

3. Single machine with thin results — A single result file that includes the results of all OVAL definitions evaluated and “thin” result types, as described in the OVAL results schema. A value of “thin” means that the minimal amount of information will be provided.
For this format, the values for the <oval-res:directives> element SHALL be:

<oval-res:directives include_source_definitions="false"> <oval-res:definition_true content="thin" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_false content="thin" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_unknown content="thin" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_error content="thin" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_not_evaluated content="thin" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_not_applicable content="thin" reported="true"/> </oval-res:directives> When specifying OVAL system characteristics, a reference SHOULD be made to the target asset in the ARF report collection. Specifically, the <oval-sc:oval_system_characteristics>/<oval-sc:system_info> SHOULD be populated with a <con:asset-identification> element. That element SHALL be populated with a single <arf:object-ref> element that points to the <ai:asset> element in the ARF report collection pertaining to the OVAL result. See [ARF] for details on populating the <arf:object-ref> element.
contents.html_ja: <oval-res:directives include_source_definitions="false"> <oval-res:definition_true content="thin" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_false content="thin" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_unknown content="thin" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_error content="thin" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_not_evaluated content="thin" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_not_applicable content="thin" reported="true"/> </oval-res:directives> OVALシステム特性を指定する際は、ARFレポートコレクション内の対象アセットへの参照を作成すべきである（SHOULD）。具体的には、<oval-sc:oval_system_characteristics>/<oval-sc:system_info>に<con:asset-identification>要素を設定すべきである（SHOULD）。その要素には、OVAL結果に関連するARFレポートコレクション内の<ai:asset>要素を指す単一の<arf:object-ref>要素を設定しなければならない（SHALL）。<arf:object-ref>要素の設定に関する詳細については、[ARF]を参照されたい。

Specifically, the <oval-sc:oval_system_characteristics>/<oval-sc:system_info> SHOULD be populated with a <con:asset-identification> element.
